subject: Notice: temporary throughput variance affecting HelionHealth API calls
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <ops@helionhealth.com>, HelionHealth SRE <sre@helionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: temporary throughput variance affecting HelionHealth API calls

Hi Samir / Helion SRE team,

I wanted to let you know we're seeing a sustained throughput variance for HelionHealth's hosted inference traffic starting ~08:50 PST this morning. Symptoms we're observing:
- elevated P95 (roughly 2-3x baseline) for text-generation endpoints used by your batch-scoring pipeline
- transient token-queueing and higher tail-retry rates for some concurrent requests
- throughput for long sequences is reduced, which is showing up as longer job completion times for your triage runs

We're treating this as a high priority. Initial mitigation we've applied:
- routed a portion of incoming requests to a warmer model variant (lower-context) to preserve throughput
- temporarily enabled a fallback routing policy to our dedicated fallback pool for heavy batch windows

Engineering is investigating root cause; early signal points to a KV cache churn event during autoscaling that caused repeated cache invalidations for a subset of model keys (attachment: ingest-logs-20281107.txt for the orchestration trace).

Next steps from our side:
1) engineering will attempt a targeted runtime patch to reduce evictions (ETA below)
2) we'll keep the fallback routing active until we confirm recovery
3) I'll share a short postmortem and a status link as soon as we have a confirmed fix

Can you confirm whether the degraded latency is affecting any live SLAs on your side (timeouts, queue backpressure), and whether you want us to enable a permanent routing to the dedicated pool while we finish the fix?

Apologies for the disruption — we're on it and will update within the hour.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <ops@helionhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 09:32:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: temporary throughput variance affecting HelionHealth API calls

Thanks for the heads up, Lauren.

Impact on our side: our nightly triage batch that kicks off at 09:00 is seeing ~40% longer processing time and a bump in 5xxs from one of the scoring jobs; some downstream workers are backing up. We're not exceeding contractual timeouts yet but the queue is building fast.

A couple quick asks:
- ETA on the runtime patch/restart?
- If you can route all scoring traffic to dedicated pool for the next 3 hours, that would help avoid cascading retries on our side.

We can temporarily increase our client-side retry backoff as well — will hold while you advise.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Ops Lead, HelionHealth
ops@helionhealth.com

Subject: Re: Notice: temporary throughput variance affecting HelionHealth API calls

On Tue, Nov 7, 2028 at 09:32 Samir Patel <ops@helionhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up, Lauren.
> ETA on the runtime patch/restart? If you can route all scoring traffic to dedicated pool for the next 3 hours, that would help.

Quick update: engineering has identified a race in the autoscaler + runtime selector that can cause repeated KV cache eviction for hot keys during a particular scale event. The result is higher cache miss rates and longer token latencies for long-context requests.

What we've done and plan to do:
- enabled full routing of HelionHealth scoring traffic to your dedicated pool (activated 09:48 PST) — this should normalize throughput for batch jobs immediately (you should see improvement within 5–10 minutes).
- applied a non-disruptive runtime selector configuration to reduce evictions for the affected key space (rolled at 09:58 PST).
- engineering is preparing a targeted patch (runtime selector guard) to fully eliminate the eviction pattern; rollout scheduled for 11:45 PST with a progressive canary and quick rollback plan.

Attached: kvcache-evict-diagram.png (simple sequence diagram) and the ingest logs we referenced.

If you prefer we can also reduce your default batch_size for the triage pipeline by 1 step from your side; that will reduce peak concurrent memory pressure while we finish the patch.

ETA for full resolution: we expect the canary and validation to finish by ~12:30 PST; if validation looks good we will promote the change cluster-wide and keep routing to the dedicated pool for an additional hour for safety.

I'll ping again as soon as the canary is validated. Thanks for the quick reply and for flagging the downstream queue.

— Lauren

Attachments: kvcache-evict-diagram.png (image/PNG)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <ops@helionhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Notice: temporary throughput variance affecting HelionHealth API calls

Hi Samir — quick confirmation from our side:

- the canary completed at 12:22 PST and we promoted the runtime selector patch across the serving fleet at 12:30 PST.
- we've kept routing to your dedicated pool for an extra hour; telemetry shows P95 back within normal bounds and token-retry rates returned to baseline.

Could you validate that your nightly triage jobs are finishing normally now and reply if you still see any residual 5xxs or queue build? We'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours.

Action items we will follow up with within 48 hours:
1) a short postmortem explaining root cause and remediation steps (will include timeline and proposed autotest to prevent regression)
2) retention of the orchestration traces used for the investigation and a sanitized log bundle (we attached the truncated ingest-logs-20281107.txt earlier)
3) an optional config change we can apply for you to keep routing to dedicated pools during nightly batches if you'd like that as a permanent mitigation

Thanks for your patience; apologies again for the disruption.

— Marissa
